claims.text: The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy does not form a continuous protective oxide layer at high temperature.
Increasing the alloy's aluminum content will enable in situ formation of an alumina scale.
The alumina scale produced by increased aluminum content will be stable, continuous, and adherent.
Added aluminum will oxidize preferentially during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential aluminum oxidation will form a dense and adherent alumina layer.
The alumina layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The oxygen-diffusion barrier will inhibit further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The aluminum-modified alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than the untreated alloy.
The aluminum-modified alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale degradation and spallation than the untreated alloy.
The predicted benefit applies during exposure at approximately 1200°C in air or pure oxygen for 100 hours.
The untreated alloy rapidly oxidizes at 1200°C in an oxidizing environment.
The untreated alloy forms non-protective scales that cause accelerated degradation.
An aluminum content that is too low may be insufficient to form a protective alumina layer.
Excessively high aluminum content may cause detrimental phase changes that impair other structural properties.
The optimal aluminum addition needed to form continuous alumina without compromising mechanical properties has not been determined.
